T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — climate risk framework integration, food price trajectory into 2026

Synopsis:
Hungary's central bank Deputy Governor flagged that the country's severe drought and expected rebound in global food prices could add to inflationary pressure in 2026. The bank is considering formally embedding climate-risk scenarios into its policy framework, though this is complicated by the mismatch between climate models' long time horizons and the bank's 18-24 month policy window. The next policy meeting is September 22, with updated quarterly forecasts due.
